chapter: With King Oliver in New York
title: First New York jobs: Sweatman trio and joining King Oliver in 1929
summary: Moore dates joining Joe Oliver to 1929, but first recounts rehearsing a trio with Wilbur Sweatman, union transfer costs, and being recruited by Dave Nelson.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Yeah. Oh, when were you with Joe Oliver? That's another thing I wanted to say.
Well, I joined Joe Oliver 1929, right here in New York. Of course, that wasn't the first job I had. The first job I had was, Wafwa was a Wilma Sweatman.

I rehearsed with him about a couple of months, especially for this job. He used, he used to use three clarinets one time. Well, there wasn't clarinets. One of them I think was, what you call that thing, O-Bo, not O-Bo, but a thing like a, uh, a- Clarinet, a Zoom? Yeah, a Zoom, clarinet. Two clarinets, a Zoom. Zoom in the middle of the mouth, two clarinets on the side. First job I had here, I think that was, a little before, around about the first, first of 29, I played with him at the Lockhead Theater. Yeah, New York. It wasn't but three of us. I was a little bit of a play.

Uh, the girl's name, the girl named Piano Fash. Used to tell what New York was, the old lady New York was the violin player. I can't remember the name. Jerry Smith? Jerry Smith, yeah, she was on the piano. And, uh, I was playing the clarinet and I was on drums. They're trio trio. He used to play a number like the roses reading them, you know. And, uh, anyway. So we rehearsed this act. About a couple of months we got it together. And, uh, we was booked in this, uh, July 5th theater. For a week. But we stayed two weeks. every stage two weeks. And I think the scale was there during that time was $55. Well, the man didn't want to pay, I have no two drummers. So he asked me, could I play the show? Yeah, I play the show. He said, well, I'll tell you what to do. He said, if you play the show, you'll make your salary $90 altogether. That was big money for me then, you know. I've never got that kind of money before. That's how I was getting around $40. So, play the show. And after I finished those two weeks, the first week, rather, the union man was there. I come in on a transfer. What you call a transfer, you know, like I belong to some other unions, don't belong to this union. But the first, the first week I worked, I don't know the man that's lacking me, I haven't taken a chance or something, what it was. Anyway, he taken, he taken half of my money to join the union. I think it was $54 to join the union. So, I think it was $35. He knew we were going to get another week, so he was going to take the rest of it, you know. So, anyway, I had to pay $54 to join the union. Then I took a visa for a while around here. King Oliver. Then, I seen this boy, Dave Nelson. Dave Nelson was King Oliver's right-hand band during that time. Dave Nelson used to do all the arranging, like music, for the band. So, he asked me, say, Boy, I said, I'd like you working very much. I see you still there, I said. I said, you want to join, join King Oliver? I said, I'm the leader of the band. I said, who? King Oliver. You ever heard of King Oliver? I said, yeah, I heard of King Oliver. You want to join? I said, yeah. How's the money? I said, we're able to talk about it, see whether he's lacking that. I said, we're going to have rehearsal tomorrow. So, he said, you come to rehearsal, see. Bring the drums. Bring the drums, yeah. Bring the drums, yeah. Bring the drums, I'm not allowed. So, I brought my drums, set them up. During that time, it had, it had 12-piece band. And, and I went too sharp on my reading. I could spell kind of slow. The most important thing, I was worried about, playing the introductions, first and second ending, and the quarter as the main thing.
